ruling.statement: Shut down all automatic AWS processes except the weekly Step Function (Saturday morning), the daily preopen and postclose Step Functions (Monday-Friday), and the 24/7 dashboard box. Everything else has its schedule removed - manual invocation only.
ruling.duration: indefinite-but-temporary ('for now'). Un-pausing is per-entry: delete the entry, run automation_pause.py --enforce is NOT needed to re-enable - re-enable explicitly with the AWS CLI or a deploy.sh reconcile.
ruling.region: us-east-1 - the only region in this account carrying EventBridge rules or Scheduler schedules (us-west-2 / us-east-2 / eu-west-1 verified empty 2026-08-07)

not_paused.alpha-engine-pipeline-watchdog-daily: pipeline watchdog - un-paused per Brian ruling 2026-08-09 (config#6697): the only same-day trading-calendar-aware liveness detector for the three KEPT pipelines; the 8/5-8/6 postclose never-fired silence had no other automatic signal. ALSO carries the weekly-SF silence deadman since config#6738 - that check was given THIS trigger rather than a new one of its own, so it needed no `pending` entry: a second schedule would have had to be born DISABLED under this ruling and then hand-enabled at the lift, leaving the 8/5-8/6 detection gap open for exactly as long as the outage that motivated it. not_paused.alpha-engine-freshness-monitor-cron: artifact freshness monitor, daily 12:00 UTC - un-paused per Brian ruling 2026-08-10 (config#6792). It is the ONLY automatic detector for a load-bearing artifact that stopped being produced by a pipeline that still SUCCEEDS. The 8/5-8/6 preopen outage was caught by the watchdog (the pipeline failed), but the class the watchdog cannot see is a green pipeline whose stage silently stopped writing - `universe_membership_latest` (severity critical, cadence weekday_sf, SLA 45min) is exactly that row, and with this cron off nothing reads it. Publishes via krepis.alerts, which is a live path since config#6751/I551.
not_paused.alpha-engine-freshness-monitor-historica: artifact freshness monitor, historical 04:00 UTC - un-paused with its two siblings per Brian ruling 2026-08-10 (config#6792). Same Lambda, same registry, different scan window; leaving it paused would have left the backfill/history rows unevaluated while the daily rows were watched, which reads as coverage the registry does not actually have.
not_paused.alpha-engine-freshness-monitor-intraday-: artifact freshness monitor, intraday every 30min 14-21 UTC Mon-Fri - un-paused with its two siblings per Brian ruling 2026-08-10 (config#6792). This is the one that catches a same-session miss inside the trading day rather than the next morning; the daily cron alone would have reported the 8/5 miss on 8/6.
not_paused.alpha-research-thinktank-daily: Think Tank daily spot dispatcher (14:30 UTC) - un-paused per Brian ruling 2026-08-10 (config#6830): the Think Tank runs ACTIVELY IN SHADOW MODE. Observe-only - its theses and challenger selections are recorded and graded, never routed into a live trading decision - and deliberately NOT part of the weekly SF (the ThinkTankCoverage chain was removed from step_function.json in the same change). This daily cadence is now the ONLY producer of thinktank_challenger_selection, which the champion/challenger loop counts as an arm: with the rule disabled that arm is a silent MISS every day. Launches one self-terminating spot box per day, bounded by THINKTANK_RUN_BUDGET_SECONDS.
not_paused.alpha-engine-expense-collector-twicedail: provider-balance + spend collector, twice daily - un-paused per Brian ruling 2026-08-11 (config#6613). not_paused.alpha-engine-router-exposure-probe-15min: model-router exposure probe, rate(15 minutes) - MOVED here from `paused.events_rules` on 2026-08-12 (alpha-engine-config-I7118). The manifest was the stale side, not AWS. Evidence, in the order it was established: CloudTrail records `EnableRule` on this name at 2026-08-12T17:38:40Z from an AdministratorAccess SSO session; `alpha-engine-config-I7002` closed 17 seconds later recording the re-enable as deliberate, with the probe's pre-enable output attached (zero violations - the edge rejects both no-credential and unknown-credential requests, the raw listener is unreachable off-host, cert 81d). I7002 also established that this rule was NOT part of Brian's I6984 deactivation: it was already DISABLED before that ruling, by something earlier and unrecorded. It is a DETECTION probe - it asserts model-router-policy R27g and takes no action - and Brian's I6984 deactivation deliberately kept detection (pipeline-watchdog, the freshness monitors, the Telegram notifiers) while pausing the response plane. Its twin alpha-engine-console-exposure-probe-15min was ENABLED throughout, so the asymmetry was drift, not policy. Codified in nous-ergon-ops/infrastructure/lambdas/router-exposure-probe/deploy.sh, NOT this repo. alpha-engine-config-I7085 deliverable 2 is done: nous-ergon-ops-PR626 (merged 2026-08-13T00:48Z, alpha-engine-config-I7129) added infrastructure/lambdas/_shared/rule_state.sh, and that deploy.sh now passes --state "$(existing_rule_state ...)" on every put-rule call rather than defaulting to ENABLED. It deliberately does NOT read this manifest - the file lives in nousergon-data and a nous-ergon-ops checkout has no reachable copy of it - so it preserves the rule's live AWS state instead, which is the manifest-independent form of the same invariant (a deploy must not change whether a schedule is running). The durable guard is still pause_reconcile.py grading this name in both directions daily.
not_paused.alpha-engine-console-exposure-probe-15mi: console exposure probe, rate(15 minutes) - the router probe's twin, verified live ENABLED and firing 96 times/day. not_paused.alpha-research-openrouter-shadow-weekly: OpenRouter shadow-judge run, cron(0 10 ? * SUN *), target alpha-engine-research-openrouter-shadow:live (alpha-engine-config#2934, crucible-research#470). FLAG FOR BRIAN - this entry records the LIVE STATE and states the open question rather than answering it. Found 2026-08-12 by the new account-wide enumeration (alpha-engine-config-I7118): live ENABLED, named in neither block of this manifest and carrying no observability registry row, with ZERO AWS/Events Invocations datapoints in the 60 days to 2026-08-12. The question is Brian's: it is a champion/challenger shadow-judge arm, and silencing an evaluation arm is the class of call he ruled on individually for the Think Tank (2026-08-10, config#6830) and the expense collector (2026-08-11, config#6613). not_paused._reactive-notifier-rules: Was a single prose key naming SIX EventPattern rules. That made it a comment by this file's own standard - `kept_names()` skips leading-underscore keys, so none of the six was asserted in either direction, and on 2026-08-12 THREE of them were measured live DISABLED while this block claimed all six were kept (alpha-engine-config-I7056). The three genuinely-enabled rules are now real keys above; the three disabled ones moved to `paused.events_rules`. A name inside a prose value is invisible to every checker - put trigger names in keys.
not_paused._non-eventbridge: DLM policy-0047cfbfb7070a3b7 (nightly dashboard-box snapshot, 14d) and the two SSM associations (ae-patch-scan-only, ae-software-inventory, rate(1 day)) are kept: they are read-only or protective hygiene for the 24/7 box, not autonomous processes.

pending._why: Triggers that do not exist live yet but MUST be created DISABLED when they first appear. Brian's ruling covers 'everything else', which includes automation that lands after 2026-08-07 — but automation_pause.py --check requires every `paused` entry to exist live, so a not-yet-created name cannot go there without turning the check red. pause_state() reads BOTH blocks; --check requires existence only for `paused`. Move an entry up to `paused` once it exists live. Found by alpha-engine-config-I6620: nousergon-data#1207 declares three schedules that its (currently broken) deploy would have created ENABLED mid-pause.
